setupIntroduction: Create your author account. Choose your own username and a password of at least 12 characters, and enter the setup key from the setup.key file you uploaded.
setupNeedsKey: Before you can create your author account, create a text file named setup.key containing one line of at least 32 random characters: this is your setup key. Upload the file into the config folder of the private folder testbraid-backend, which must be outside your public folder (the folder web browsers can open). Then check setup again.
setupAlreadyCompleted: The first author has already been created. Refresh the page and sign in.
setupNotEnabled: No setup key was found. Upload setup.key into testbraid-backend/config and try again.
usernameRules: Letters without accents, digits, dots, dashes or underscores. No spaces.
usernameInvalid: This username cannot be used. Use only letters without accents, digits, dots, dashes or underscores, and no spaces.

securityDiagnosticsIntro: Optional checks of where the private folder (testbraid-backend) is placed. Findings do not block the application; you decide how to address them.
securityCheckFailed: The check failed. Verify your author session and API availability.
securityPlacement_within-public-app: Warning: located inside the public folder of this application.
securityPlacement_within-inferred-site-r: Warning: probably located inside your site's public folder.
securityPlacement_outside-inferred-site-: Outside your site's public folder, as far as can be detected.
securityPlacement_unverified: Unable to verify the folder layout.
securityApacheRulePresent: A deny directive was found (its effectiveness is not verified).
securityApacheRuleMissing: No recognizable deny directive or .htaccess was found.
securityProbeMissing: Missing. For the HTTP test, upload security-probe.txt from the ZIP's testbraid-backend folder into your private folder.
securityInconclusive: These checks cannot prove complete security. Apache may have aliases or may ignore .htaccess.
securityProbeUrl: Path to the probe file on this domain
securityProbeExplanation: Enter a path only if you know it. It must start with / and end in /security-probe.txt. Example: /testbraid-backend/security-probe.txt. Example text is not a prefilled value.
securityProbe_exposed: RISK: the test file can be opened in a web browser, so other private files can be too. Move the private folder out of the public folder.
securityProbe_blocked: This specific URL did not serve the file (HTTP 403 or 404). Other URLs may still expose it.
securityProbe_unverified: Inconclusive: the server neither served the expected file nor unambiguously denied access.
securityProbe_invalid: Invalid path. Enter a same-origin path starting with / and ending in /security-probe.txt, without parameters or ../.
securityOverviewGood: The private folder and its data appear to be placed appropriately.
securityOverviewDanger: Warning: some private files are located inside the application's public folder.
securityOverviewWarning: Security is inconclusive or the folder layout needs further checking.
securityOverviewExposed: Confirmed exposure: the probe file is accessible over HTTP.
securityOverviewNote: This is advisory only. It cannot detect every web-server alias or later configuration change.
securityAdvancedHttpTitle: Advanced: test a specific HTTP URL (optional)
securityAdvancedHttpIntro: If you know a URL that might open files from the private folder, you can test whether the server serves its harmless probe file. This is optional and cannot prove that all paths are protected.
securityNoSuggestedUrl: The private folder is outside the detected public folder, so the application cannot suggest a URL for it. Leave this empty if you do not know one.
securitySuggestedUrl: The application derived this possible URL from the private folder's location. You can keep or change it:
mediaDropMultiple: Drop files here or browse files
mediaUploadResult: Uploaded {uploaded} of {total} files. Failed files can be retried.
demoBanner: This is a read-only demo of TestBraid. To create your own tests, install TestBraid on your own web hosting.
